scale_policy: Keep physical specimen calibration separate from independent cell/nucleus/pore/vasa/adipose teaching enlargements; attach local badges to all enlarged examples.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Circumferential smooth-muscle activation changes lumen radius against passive wall and distending pressure.

steps.text: Inspect a section and follow the long axes of visible smooth-muscle cells around the lumen; each selected nucleus belongs to its cell.
Compare reference tone and increased activation at a stated fixed distending pressure; shortening is circumferential and intimal layers move coherently with the lumen boundary.
Compare reduced activation with the reference state; distinguish this active change from a passive pressure change.
Show an ideal segment comparison using R proportional to r^-4 and Q proportional to r^4 at fixed pressure difference, length and viscosity.

state_or_cue_design.continuous_controls: Do not expose an unvalidated deformation slider.

schematic_limitations: Ideal flow assumes straight rigid circular tube, steady laminar flow and Newtonian viscosity; this artery is compliant and pulsatile.
This segment distributes flow; small arteries/arterioles contribute strongly to resistance and systemic pressure is a network result.
Do not impose constant outer radius or collapse the lumen; wall volume/thickness response requires separate mechanical validation.
Cell and nuclear examples are enlarged sampling, not literal cell counts.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Endothelial stimulus, diffusible NO, smooth-muscle sGC/cGMP signaling and reduced contractile activation.

steps.text: Orient the blood-facing continuous cellular lining and its supported basal surface.
Present shear/receptor stimulus as a teaching cue on an endothelial cell; activate NO production.
Trace a short-lived diffusible signal into a nearby medial smooth-muscle cell.
Show sGC/cGMP as a molecular inset and reduced smooth-muscle activation; return to the larger lumen state panel.

state_or_cue_design.colors: Use a signal-specific legend distinct from red/blue blood vessels.
state_or_cue_design.animation: Optional timed highlighting; no claimed concentration solver.

schematic_limitations: NO is an example of endothelial signaling; EDH, prostacyclin and contracting factors are not simulated.
Diffusion crosses tissue, not an open blood conduit through the IEL.
Acetylcholine experimental relaxation does not establish parasympathetic innervation of all arteries.
Times and signal ranges are illustrative.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Sympathetic varicosity release, local NE diffusion, alpha-1 activation and smooth-muscle calcium-dependent contraction.

steps.text: Follow an adventitial axon to connected varicosities beside the represented outer medial muscle.
Highlight impulse arrival, release from more than one varicosity and a short local matrix gap.
Show NE binding alpha-1 receptors on smooth muscle; the inset links PLC/IP3-related calcium signaling to calcium/calmodulin and MLCK.
Return to circumferential cellular shortening and the narrowed lumen panel; allow withdrawal of activation to return toward the reference state.

state_or_cue_design.junction: diffuse neuroeffector relation with visible gap; no motor endplate

schematic_limitations: NE route chosen for clarity; ATP and NPY cotransmission is acknowledged.
Innervation/receptor distribution and terminal depth vary by vessel bed; no absolute never-in-media rule.
Do not draw axons targeting nuclei or branching to every visible muscle cell.
No physiological firing frequency, NE concentration, latency or receptor density is claimed.

functional_sequences.mechanism: IEL fenestration is a real interruption through an elastic sheet and permits communication across the intima-media boundary.

steps.text: Isolate one enlarged opening and show its rim and passage through the lamina thickness.
Restore adjacent layers so luminal support and the medial muscle identify the two sides.
Show a diffusible communication cue; optionally open a separately labeled research inset containing one endothelial projection and a myoendothelial junction.
Restore the representative IEL and remind the learner that these are sparsely displayed rat-prior enlarged examples.

state_or_cue_design.pore_disclosure: 20 times rat popliteal diameter prior; sparse examples; not human morphometry
state_or_cue_design.endothelial_boundary: Keep continuous; an IEL opening is not an endothelial fenestra.

schematic_limitations: Not every opening contains a myoendothelial junction.
Rat segment/bed data do not calibrate human arterial pores or density.
EEL apertures must not inherit IEL morphometry.
No blood cell or bulk flow passes through these holes in the healthy-wall lesson.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Distinct luminal diffusion and outer-wall vasa exchange serve living wall tissue; venules and optional lymphatics drain different compartments.

steps.text: Separate the main lumen through-flow from the nutrition of its own wall.
Trace arterial vasa from a specimen inlet into a branching wall capillary exchange region.
Show oxygen/nutrient diffusion from luminal blood toward inner wall and from capillary blood toward served outer wall, with tissue consumption and no fixed exclusive radial boundary.
Trace capillary-to-venular continuity and an explicit venous specimen exit.
In an optional outer connective-tissue inset, trace interstitial fluid/solute drainage into a separate lymphatic route.

state_or_cue_design.transport_cues: blood along vessels; solute across microvessel boundary; diffusion into tissue
state_or_cue_design.lymphatic_if_not_built: Mark lymphatic drainage as not displayed instead of implying venular equivalence.

schematic_limitations: Predominantly adventitial representative placement is specimen-specific; larger muscular arteries may have outer-medial vasa.
No universal inner-third/outer-two-thirds boundary or oxygen concentration values.
Wall diffusion is neither radial blood flow nor leakage of blood cells.
Lymphatic caliber/density and venular reabsorption fractions are not calibrated.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Pressure-induced distension loads elastic matrix and progressively recruits collagen, distinct from active muscle tone.

steps.text: Hold muscle activation conceptually fixed and compare passive distension states.
Follow elastic boundaries and connective support deforming with the wall.
Track selected initially wavy adventitial bundles becoming straighter and sharing greater tensile load as stretch increases.
Return to reference pressure and explain recoil and matrix constraint alongside the active tone sequence.

state_or_cue_design.collagen: coherent bundles seated in common adventitial connective tissue
state_or_cue_design.variables: pressure changes distinguished from tone changes
state_or_cue_design.numerics: No threshold pressure or maximum radius assigned.

schematic_limitations: Recruitment is progressive and vessel/state dependent; collagen is not slack until one universal high pressure.
No universal material modulus, constitutive model or guaranteed reversible path is claimed.
Six large bundles sample course; they do not stand in for all matrix architecture.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Perivascular adipose context can modulate local vascular tone through context-dependent paracrine pathways.

steps.text: Identify an adipocyte in outer connective tissue by lipid-dominated cell body, thin cytoplasmic rim and eccentric nucleus.
Show a local signal cue from this environment toward vascular tissue, with an example of adiponectin-associated NO bioavailability in human small-artery research.
Optionally compare a clearly labeled research-context panel where inflammatory/hypoxic adipose loses this anticontractile effect.
Return to the normal specimen and distinguish chemical modulation from mechanical padding.

state_or_cue_design.factor: adiponectin/NO shown as example, not sole universal pathway
state_or_cue_design.scale: Adipocyte geometry enlarged independently; disclose alongside displayed specimen.

schematic_limitations: Human gluteal small-artery results do not determine every vascular bed or adipose depot.
Obesity does not impose a deterministic outcome on every artery.
No edema, plaque, concentration or inflammatory timeline is simulated.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Activated arterial endothelium may support selectin-mediated transient leukocyte rolling; arrest/transmigration are conditional further events.

steps.text: Enable the explicitly labeled inflamed-arterial-endothelium lesson; orient the blood-facing contact.
Show temporary selectin-ligand attachments forming ahead and releasing behind while the cell translates and rotates.
Display a transient detachment branch; rolling need not progress to adhesion.
Offer a separate molecular inset explaining that chemokine-induced integrin activation can support arrest; no automatic wall traversal in this artery.
Exit the inflammatory lesson and restore healthy opening visibility with the leukocyte hidden.

state_or_cue_design.cell_identity: neutrophil retained from source; segmented nucleus inset

schematic_limitations: Classical routine emigration lesson belongs mainly to postcapillary venules; arterial case is an illustrative inflammatory exception.
Primary observation was atherosclerotic mouse aorta; it does not calibrate this human-representative geometry.
No rolling velocity, bond force, shear threshold or inevitable arrest/diapedesis is claimed.
Static cell adjacency alone must not be labeled demonstrated rolling.
